summary.text: Amanda Pusczek, a Democrat and registered nurse, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Alabama's 4th Congressional District to Robert Aderholt.
According to her campaign website, she was born in Missouri, grew up in Alabama, and has more than a decade of clinical nursing experience, including psychiatric nursing.
She had not previously held elected office and described herself as a nurse rather than a career politician, campaigning on health care and cost-of-living issues.

paragraphs.text: According to her campaign website, Pusczek was born in 1990 in Ferguson, Missouri, and moved to Alabama with her mother at age six, with a few years spent in Wiesbaden, Germany. She told a Walker County Democratic meeting in January 2026 that she was born in Missouri in 1990; her Ballotpedia survey profile lists Alabama as her birthplace.

She graduated from public school with an Advanced Diploma in 2008, then earned an Associate Degree in Nursing at John C. Calhoun Community College, which Ballotpedia lists as 2014, and a bachelor's degree from Western Governors University in 2022.

Pusczek works as a nurse with more than a decade of clinical experience and a stated interest in psychiatric nursing and mental health advocacy. Her campaign website says she traveled to New York City during the COVID-19 outbreak while completing her bachelor's degree in nursing, and she told the Walker County meeting that her work has included hospitals, prisons and schools.

She married her husband in 2022. Her campaign website says Alabama's health-care and reproductive-rights restrictions affected the couple's family plans, and the Mountain Eagle reports that this and the 2024 election contributed to her decision to run.
Pusczek has no prior campaigns or offices listed on Ballotpedia. She won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for the 4th District, defeating Shane Weaver, 62.8% to 37.2%.
She is affiliated with the American Nurses Association, 50501, the Madison County Democratic Party, Alabama Young Democrats, and Indivisible 5th District North Alabama.
She received 25.1% of the vote to Robert Aderholt's 74.9%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
